# MCP servers

> **Disabled by default.** MCP servers are a preview area and are off by default; enable with
> `CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true` and restart CALIBER (the same flag turns on OpenAPI integrations). While
> it is off, the `/mcp-servers*` routes answer 404 (`reason_code: feature_disabled`), the MCP Servers page is
> hidden, and a workflow MCP node is reported as unavailable ("A registered MCP server that CALIBER can reach (needs CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true)"). Enabling the
> flag means you accept preview behavior. See [Feature flags](m-61-alpha-scope.md#feature-flags).

Use this page when the practical question is how to connect CALIBER to an MCP
server, verify the discovered tools, and govern what remote tools may do.

## At a glance

| Task | Start here | Deep reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| register or configure a server | define connection and transport details | [MCP architecture](m-05-mcp.md) |
| verify tool discovery | inspect the discovered inventory | [MCP architecture](m-05-mcp.md) |
| govern remote actions | apply approval and policy boundaries | [Trust and governance](m-33-trust-and-governance.md) |
| use MCP tools in assistant or workflows | wire them into the target surface | [Aria assistant](m-46-use-aria-assistant.md), [Workflows](m-42-use-workflows.md) |

## 1. What MCP adds to CALIBER

MCP lets CALIBER connect to externally hosted tool surfaces without baking each
integration directly into the core product. That increases power, but it also
raises the need for connection tests, inventories, and policy enforcement.

A server uses one of three transports: `stdio`, `sse` or `streamable-http`. The workflow from the API is
`POST /mcp-servers`, then `POST /mcp-servers/{server_id}/test-connection`, then
`POST /mcp-servers/{server_id}/discover-tools`, then a per-tool policy with
`PATCH /mcp-servers/{server_id}/tools/{tool_name}/policy`.

**A discovered tool is denied until you classify it.** Discovery establishes that the tool exists, not that
it may run: with no policy a tool is `allowed: false`. The policy carries `allowed`, `side_effect_level` and
`requires_approval`, and an allowed tool whose `side_effect_level` is `write` or `external_action` must set
`requires_approval` (the PATCH answers 400 otherwise). A local `stdio` server is containment, not isolation;
only a managed sidecar or a non-loopback HTTPS endpoint counts as an external execution boundary when a
production-class alias is promoted.

A remote server's address is checked against the egress policy as well as the host allowlist, so an
endpoint on `127.0.0.1` or a private network address is refused by default ("resolves into the blocked
loopback range") even though the allowlist names loopback. Run a server on the CALIBER host over `stdio`:
the command must be on `CALIBER_MCP_STDIO_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST`, and a Python script must be an allowlisted
`-m` module or an absolute path in `CALIBER_MCP_STDIO_PYTHON_SCRIPT_ALLOWLIST`. The
[Governed Tool Connectivity lab](cookbooks/05-mcp-connectivity-governance-lab/README.md)
runs a real one.

**Your policy, not the server's word, decides what a tool may do.** A server reports its own tool names, descriptions and
hints such as `readOnlyHint`; CALIBER treats all of it as data and never as a classification. In a workflow, a tool you
classified `read` runs inline; a tool you classified `write` or `external_action` is proposed, approved by an exact approval and
dispatched once (and left `unknown`, never resent, if the server's answer is lost, because most MCP servers cannot confirm their
own effects); a tool you have not classified, or blocked, is refused with a code such as `mcp_tool_unclassified` before anything
is sent. The first-party database server's write tools are refused in a workflow. See
[Governed MCP tools](m-64-reference-profile.md#governed-mcp-tools-b045) for the exact codes and recovery.

Inside a project, creating, changing or deleting a server and changing a tool policy need the global
`caliber.admin` scope and `editor` or `owner`. Testing the connection, discovering tools and invoking a tool
need `caliber.admin` and `reviewer`, `editor` or `owner`. Saving a tool's test cases needs `caliber.operator`
and `editor` or `owner`, and calibrating a tool needs `caliber.operator` and `reviewer` or above. A member with
too weak a role gets 403 and a person outside the project gets 404.

## 3. Common failure modes

| Symptom | First thing to check |
| --- | --- |
| There is no MCP Servers page, or a call answers 404 with `reason_code: feature_disabled` | `CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS` is off (the default); set it to `true` and restart |
| The server connects but tools do not appear | discovery or transport mismatch |
| Tools appear but cannot run | the tool has no policy yet (the default is denied), or it needs approval, or its secret-source configuration is wrong |
| The same tool behaves differently across environments | endpoint, credentials, or server version drift |
